explicit_definitions_given: Three-dimensionalism: objects have extension in three dimensions and persist by enduring
Four-dimensionalism: objects have temporal parts and persist by perduring
Proper part: x is a proper part of y iff x is a part of y and y is not a part of x
Form: principle of unity of a thing; functional explanation

objections_raised: Region relativization already accounts for configuration
Maximal properties could solve the problem
Clay and statue both occupy the same region

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Problem of the many, material constitution, parthood, form

structural_organization.structure_type: Sectioned with numbered sections and a conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The paper identifies a fatal flaw in Hudson's 3d Partist View (Tibbles problem) and proposes a five-place parthood relation that includes a form (in-F relation). This Hylomorphic Partism distinguishes constituters from constituted objects by appealing to form as a principle of unity, thereby solving the problem of the many without abandoning three-dimensionalism. The author defends the view against objections concerning superfluousness, maximal properties, and co-location.

thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low: states the view resolves problems and aligns with everyday beliefs
